debrief_start: ^Shutdown engaged before the racks went. Banks isolated, hall intact.
^Bank B went before I reached the button. Shutdown held A and C.
^He reached the laptop before I reached him. Shutdown held A and C.

b: ^Bank B's gone, but you isolated A and C and forced the vents. It could have been the whole hall. It wasn't.
^Clean. Runaway aborted before a single cell vented. Banks isolated.
^And Voltage got out through the dock.

debrief_attack_stopped: ^What did we get out of there?

b: ^Vance lost nine of his crew tonight. He hasn't said a word about you yet.
^Vance says you kept it to one bank. He still wants that in writing.
^Vance says the grid held because of you. He wants that in writing.
^The facility manager's being treated by medics. He'll live. He won't be filing a commendation.
^And the gate guard's in A&E with a sore head. He was the one person on site doing his job by the book.
^Good. Nobody else in that building knows the chain above Blackout.
^He'll talk. Men like him always want to explain themselves.
^A shame. But the attack's stopped, and that was the job.
^The intelligence you brought out is the proof we've been chasing since the Zero Day job.

debrief_intelligence_gathered: ^The directive said it: Zero Day supplies, Critical Mass executes, grid storage this winter. Tonight was that plan, running.

b: ^Voltage is in a room now. So far he's given us one thing: his casualty figure.
^Voltage is gone, so the paper will have to talk.
^And his print on that bypass module puts his own hand in the cabinet. That'll stand up in court.
^His print's on that bypass module. When someone does find him, it'll be waiting.
^Cipher went to look at the night crew and kept walking. Police picked him up on the access road. He's talking.
^The documents show Critical Mass and Social Fabric coordinating the one attack, in their own handwriting.
^Their FTP drop already put Critical Mass and Social Fabric on the same job. The paper in the plant room would have signed it.
^And that card from the go-bag. It decodes to Calder Wharf, Social Fabric's regional safehouse. That goes on the board.

debrief_intelligence_gathered: ^Keep the crew's fingerprint kit. Forensics can have the case.
^And how did they get in? How did I?
debrief_what_failed: ^Agent HaX: Before you write it up. Three things let them in. Two of them let you in too.

b: ^Agent HaX: Vance's door card copied from across his own desk. Old prox hands its number to anything that asks.
^Agent HaX: Their door cards are old prox. They hand their number to anything that asks. You could have had Vance's from across his desk.
^Agent HaX: You did it to Relay too, while she was talking.

debrief_what_failed: ^Agent HaX: The HV door took one finger, and that finger was on a panel he touched every two hours. A print names you. It can't prove you're the one standing there.
^Agent HaX: And the control room believed its own sensors. The honest instruments were the ones nobody had wired to the bus: a dial, and a gas monitor nobody read.
^Agent HaX: On the network it was the same story.
^Agent HaX: A legacy compile service left running on an OT box, trusting whatever it was sent.
^Agent HaX: An FTP service that handed their cross-cell plan to anyone who looked. And an account on the jump server with far more privilege than its job needed.
^Agent HaX: Encrypted cards. A second factor on the HV door, and a reader that checks for a live finger.
^Agent HaX: A temperature gauge in every hall that isn't on the bus, and somebody reading it.
^Agent HaX: Old services off the OT network, and privileges somebody actually reviews.
^It goes in the report. Vance will want every line.
^The budget let them in as much as the readers did.

c-2: ^Agent HaX: Put that in too. It's the line nobody upstairs will want to read.

debrief_big_picture: ^Social Fabric had disinformation ready in three cities, to turn the fire into a panic.
^The Architect. He's running all of it.
debrief_architect_revelation: ^The same name the Zero Day directive carried. The Architect.
^We've just watched one of his strikes run start to finish. Now we know how the cells fit together.
^This site was a rehearsal. The real thing is bigger, and it's coming.

b:
^Voltage told you six cities, in the plant room.

^OptiGrid, their cover firm, has contracts at forty sites nationwide. We're auditing every one.

^The documents name several cities.

^OptiGrid's contracts turn up at dozens of infrastructure sites.

debrief_scale_explanation: ^We've never seen it run this tight.
debrief_task_force_announcement: ^Netherton wants a standing team on The Architect. Hunt the coordination, not the cells.
^He's calling it Task Force Null. Your name's on his list.
task_force_mission_explanation: ^Find whoever sends the directives. Every cell we've hit so far was working from the same ones.
^Four missions now, and you're still standing. The last of them nearly didn't go that way.
task_force_accepted: ^He'll call when he's ready. Not tonight.

b: ^Agent HaX: The banks are isolated, but he got to the laptop before you got to him, and Bank B went with it.
^Agent HaX: The banks are isolated, but Bank B went before you got to the button.

^Agent HaX: Nine on the night crew in Hall 2. Two more on the feed before the grid caught up.

^Agent HaX: You stopped the rest of it. Hold on to that, because the number you read tomorrow won't be zero.

^Agent HaX: Your alarm started his clock. Bank B and two on the feed are what it cost.

^Agent HaX: Nine people in Hall 2 are what it bought. Hall 2 was empty when it went.

^Agent HaX: Hall 2 was empty when it went. Vance's alarm had the night crew out through the fire doors.

^Agent HaX: Two on the feed before the grid caught up. The number tomorrow won't be zero. It won't be eleven either.
^Agent HaX: Everyone on site got out alive tonight, not all of them on their own feet. Forty-odd on that feed never knew they were on it.
^Agent HaX: Eleven people walked out of there tonight. Forty-odd on that feed never knew they were on it.
^Agent HaX: And Vance's alarm had the night crew out before the button went in. It started your clock early. It was still the right call.
^Agent HaX: And Vance's alarm had the night crew out before the button went in.

disclosure_decision: ^Full public disclosure. People have a right to know.
^Keep it classified. Let them patch it quietly.
^Say there was an incident. Keep the details back.
disclosure_full_public: ^Full transparency. The attack, the holes it came through, ENTROPY. All of it.

b: ^Robert Vance: It'll hurt us. People should still know how close it came.
^Robert Vance: There'll be hell to pay for this place. Fair enough.

disclosure_full_public: ^The public gets the truth and the warning with it. Albion takes the hit, every other storage site gets audited, and someone in Parliament finally answers for the funding.
disclosure_quiet: ^We classify it. A maintenance fault, resolved. Albion patches the holes quietly.

b: ^Robert Vance: I'll keep my mouth shut. Doesn't mean I like it. Those people are on our feed.
^Robert Vance: Good. One more headline and they'd close us.

disclosure_quiet: ^Nobody hears how close this came. Albion's name survives, the upgrades happen, and nothing makes the rest of the sector move. Stability, bought with silence.

b: ^Robert Vance: Something, not everything. I can live with that.
^Robert Vance: That'll go down well upstairs, I suppose.

disclosure_partial: ^People hear something happened, not all of it. Enough to push some change, not enough to start a panic.

b: ^Statement goes out with the local authorities.
^A controlled statement goes to the press.
^Robert Vance: I don't know what you are. I know what you did.
^Robert Vance: Nine of mine. I'll be telling their families myself.
^Robert Vance: You kept it to one bank. Without you it was the whole hall.
^Robert Vance: Nobody in that hall died, and two hundred and forty thousand never lost the lights.

^Robert Vance: You did right by this place.

^Robert Vance: I'll not forget it.
^Robert Vance: I don't follow all of it. I know the hall's still standing.

disclosure_outcome: ^It was an honour working with you, Mr Vance.
^Make sure the site manager gets the report.
^Make sure Vance gets the full credit when he comes round.
debrief_end_respectful: ^Robert Vance: We've run this place on hope and gaffer tape for years.
^Robert Vance: That stops on my shift.
debrief_end_professional: ^Robert Vance: I'll have those card readers out by the end of the week.
debrief_end_not_met: ^He'll get it. He'll want to know who was in his plant tonight, and why nobody told him.
debrief_end_ko: ^Noted. It'll be in the report either way.
^The methods are a separate conversation. You put a facility manager on the floor of his own office tonight.

b: ^Voltage is out there. So is The Architect.
^All three of his crew down. Thorough.
^And not one of his crew on the floor. Harder than it looks.
